items.title: Al Gallodoro Interview, 1966-05-10
items.q: you will notice Irving Berman, unfair list, Manor Records, unfair list.

ctx.x: Son of a gun. I'll play for you tomorrow night. Oh my God, it's a collector's item. I can go on and on. Take it on tape, that's all right. We got it. All right. Whiteman commissioned this for me and the reason it was called concerto for doubles in the band, I played alto, clarinet, and bass clarinet. So we had a special broadcast one night where I played the three instruments and I did like oodles and oodles on sax, I did the Flight of the Bumblebee on clarinet. And I believe I did something on bass clarinet, I…
That's the one with the picture of the saxophone on the cover.

items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: We each put up $1,350... Sam, Irving Berman was the other fellow.

ctx.x: Yeah. I think I do. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

You have it. Well we hired a 50 piece orchestra. We each put up $1,350. The session started right in Carnegie Hall at midnight. And we went until six in the morning. And I did the whole three movements of the “Concerto for Doubles.” Alto sax, bass clarinet, clarinet. Then I did “Oodles of Noodles” and the “Fantasy Impromptu.” But I was in my prime then. 50 piece orchestra. My brother Frank was in the band. And I went to the office one day and he gave me a check for about $240. He says, “I’m going to send Ralph…
Yes. In fact I wanted to play just a brief thing here for you, okay? Let me see if I can get this piece up and perhaps you can tell me a little bit about it. We’ll just listen to.
